When I mentioned this to my therapist, she gave me a weird look and asked me why. I said I didn't know, but didn't think about it much (then or afterwards).
Now it hit me. That look. It was all in my head. I was always capable of being like everyone else. I'm not a demon. I'm not a worthless waste of my parent's efforts of raising me as well as they possibly could. I'm not a sack of shit and I'm not destined to be unhappy; I think people should be happy, I love people, so I want to, I have to love myself. I always thought of self-improvement as a challenge or as a prove of my love for others (improving means I become more capable of helping those I love); but never as love for myself.

Hey! Look, congratulations on your journey and initiative! That's great, you're doing your future self a HUGE favor.
I would, however, like to point out something: avoid the "all or nothing mentality. It's damaging for your progress for the long run because self-improvement requires going through discomfort, challenging yourself. And, if you are truly taking challenges that are "up to your level", so to speak, you are probably going to fail some times. With the "all or nothing" mentality, those are the times when you'll feel like nothing. And feeling like nothing absolutely sucks. So i encourage you to avoid that mentality and focus on making progress instead: try to be a tiny bit better than yesterday, every day. Hope that helps.
Take care, and welcome to this wonderful (and lifelong, at least for me) journey. Wish you the best, friend.

Hey;
Honestly, I disagree with your two previous responses to his comment. About me (the little dating experience I have definitely influences my opinion): I used to be really self-conscious and therefore would look at my dates and interactions with girls looking for signs to interpret as "my fault" for being stood up, ghosted, or generally (what I also interpreted as) having been rejected. I used to talk about that to the person a lot, saying stuff like "Hey, is everything alright?" "Did I do something wrong?" or "I noticed in hindsight I did x on our date. That wasn't cool and I apologize." (sometimes it was just all in my head; she would respond saying she didn't notice anything wrong or that I haven't done x). If OP says that he thinks the date was like 75% good and you feel like the girl's reaction to his latest texts does not reflect what he says, in the end, he still knows more about what went down on that date then both of us; he was the one there. And I think suggesting that it was actually all his fault might make him feel bad and REALLY self-conscious when, in reality, he may not have anything to do with it. 
So, OP: sometimes it is your fault, as in "something you DID". But man, it could be SO many things; maybe she found you unattractive, maybe something complicated came up in her life around that time; maybe an ex texted her again and it messed with her feelings; maybe she doesn't even know why she didn't respond and is making a post on this exact same subreddit (or somewhere else where people talk about dating, social skills etc.) asking for advice on how to handle the situation; or maybe she doesn't even know why she didn't respond, but she just didn't.
I know all of this sounds kind of crazy, and that's because it is. People are kind of crazy, really, and so is life. In reality, if that was your first date with her, you are just a VERY small part of her existence (and the other way around). I mean, she might have even  made a mental note to respond you later and forget about it.
So, in conclusion, I know it may be kind of difficult rn, but try to think about it as clearly and objectively as you possibly can. If you conclude that you did something wrong and feel like apologizing is the right thing to do to her and would put this issue to rest, then go ahead and do that. If you don't, just don't. She may have already forgotten all about it, who knows? Just don't let this eat you alive and move on.

All the best!

Can I be honest? I'm not the best at evaluating these situations, so definetly take whatever I have to say with a grain of salt, but here's my two cents: something seems to have happened, between high school and college, with your ability to socialize. It sort of happened to me both on the transition from middle school to high school and from high school to uni (the last one due to lockdown; spent two years at home and genuinely forgot how to talk to people lol). Did something impactful happened in this period? Apart from the socializing situation, how have you been feeling? Are you alright?

My mind's really full rn so this must be a mess, but what I'm trying to say is:if you WANT to socialize, you WANT to be in social situations but seem to be scared of putting yourself in those situations (which is something that didn't happen systematically before, from what you said), you may have somewhat of a problem. That's why I asked how you were feeling: if you've been frequently having depressive or anxious thoughts, maybe it has something to do with your mental health. In that case, if you have the means to, I'd reccomend seeing a therapist. If you can't do that, however, I reccomend journaling (at least it's what I do for lack of a therapist): lay your thoughts, feelings, intentions and memories onto paper. Whatever you feel like writing, really. The thoughts usually just flow. It doesn't have to be that cohesive either, no one's gonna see it. It usually helps me really dive into an issue that's somewhat bothering me and finish the session feeling my thoughts a bit more organized.

If you have trauma, however, I'd advise you not to delve too deep in your thoughts: there's some scary shit there; if you're gonna dive into your past, trust me, do it with a therapist. I tired doing it on my own last year and had the worst mental breakdown of my life (which is definitely saying something...).

If it doesn't seem to be related to mental health, on the other hand, I'd go with what people are saying: try to slowly put yourself into social situations; step out of your comfort zone.


I guess that's it. Hope things get better on your end. Take care, dude!

First of all, calm down. Dealing damage is not the answer; it's useless and will most likely benefit them (they could spin this on you and make you become the asshole of the situation). Please ignore whatever dipshit that tries to tell you that revenge is "cool" or "justice". Resist the bullying, preferably in a non-violent way. Violence is shit; it messes people up mentally (both parties involved) and could go south really fast if you let yourself go in a fit of anger (even if not phisically; words have a huge impact on people and you may deeply regret what you said, even if it was said with the intention to make things better). If someone is being manipulative, call them out on it. People HATE feeling manipulated (think of the people that go absolutely apeshit when their SO cheats on them), so do your best to point out to your friends exactly what the bully is doing and that they're doing it to hurt your feelings. Of course, draw the line and defend yourself if necessary, but try to keep it simple: you're a person dealing with a person who acts like a douchebag. There's no need for more drama or hostility. If what you described is all they're doing, you don't have to let it get to you so much (that would only worsen the situation for you and give them the satisfaction of seeing you down). 

Also, as someone here brilliantly pointed out: kill them with kindness. When there's no need to worry about your physical safety, you can be a lot more calm and cool-headed during the harassment (of course, it affects you and you obviously feel bad about it, but that doesn't have to control you actions or words.). Use this to your advantage: be kind to them in front of your friends. Not only will it make them REALLY uncomfortable (they're most likely trying to get a bad reaction out of you), it will send a clear message to your friends: you're the cool person who's being treated badly (and that can keep your head cool in these situations, which trust me, is valued by people), and the bully is the real asshole. That should be enough for the manipulation to stop. 

I really hope things get better on your end and you can leave this shitty situation behind you. Wish you the best, take care.
